evidence.quote: The problem here is the standard odd-primary Adams-family problem; the classical prime-two Kervaire invariant one problem has a different family and dimension convention.

exclusions.query: Kervaire invariant one problem at the prime two
exclusions.reason: The paper treats the odd-primary Adams family only.

evidence.quote: For every odd prime $p\geq5$, it excludes all standard Kervaire classes $b_j$ with $j\geq1$

exclusions.query: survival of b_j at primes at least five
exclusions.reason: Non-existence there is quoted from prior work, not proved here.

One has $0,2\in K_3$ and $1\notin K$.

Let $j\geq2$, and let $\alpha\in\pi_{4\cdot3^{j+1}-2}S_{(3)}$ be detected by $b_j$ in the mod-$3$ Adams spectral sequence.
Let a finite group $J$ act on a characteristic-zero domain $A$ and semilinearly on a free rank-one module $Ae$.
Let a finite group $J$ act coherently on a spectrum $Z$.
For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, the group $\pi_{-2n}(E^{hG})$ contains an element of infinite additive order.
Suppose that the graded groups $\pi_*(E^{hG})$ are $972$-periodic and that $\pi_{-2}(E^{hG})$ is torsion-free.
Let $F^{s+1}\to F^s$, $s\geq0$, be a decreasing tower of spectra, or of genuine spectra for a finite group.
In the cofree genuine spectra associated to $E$, the actual faithful Euler classes satisfy $$a_{\lambda|H}^{79}=0,\qquad a_\lambda^{235}=0.$$
For $1\le i\le5$, the operator $D_g$ sends $P_i$ into the span of $P_0,\ldots,P_{i-1}$, with a nonzero coefficient of $P_{i-1}$.

There is an isomorphism of trigraded algebras $$\label{coef:first-page}
 \mathcal E_1
 =k[b^{\pm1},u^{\pm1},N_0,N_1,N_2]
       \otimes\Lambda(e,z_0,z_1,z_2).$$

After compatible nonzero scalar normalizations, the auxiliary coefficient spectral sequence has $$d_1(u)=uz_0,\qquad
 d_1(e)=ez_0,\qquad
 d_1(z_i)=z_i z_0\ (i=1,2),\qquad d_1(z_0)=0.$$
Set $x_i=g^i x_0$, with indices read modulo nine.
Put $q_i=\mathop{\mathrm{N}}_H(x_i)$, $q=q_0$.
On every nonzero topological Tate page, $$A=qb^{-2}$$ is a permanent-cycle unit, and every element of $K$ is a cycle.
Let $B$ be an Artinian local ring with residue characteristic three, and let $F_1,F_2$ be deformations over $B$ of formal groups of finite height.
The eigenvalue condition $$\sigma x_i=\zeta x_i$$ defines a framed strict formal $\mathcal O$-module deformation space of relative height three.
Every open subgroup of $\mathcal C$ has infinite image on $D'$.
A nonzero invariant meromorphic section of $w^i$ is a constant multiple of $h^d$, where $8d=-i$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$.

After a finite extension of constants there is an equivariant isomorphism $$\label{coef:determinant-formula}
 \det(D'\otimes_{S_0}W)\cong w^{-9}\chi,$$ where $\chi:\mathcal C\to\{\pm1\}$ is a sign character whose restriction to $T$ has weight $13$, and is therefore nontrivial.
For every integer $n$, including after meromorphic localization, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal C,S_0}(W,P_n)=0.$$

With compatible nonzero scalar normalizations, the images of the indicated Greek-letter classes are $$\alpha_1=\theta,\qquad
  \beta_1=bJ,\qquad
  \beta_{3/3}=bJ^3,\qquad

On the cohomology of [h:sector-complex], the operation $\kappa=A^2d_9$ preserves both the $A$- and $b$-exponents and lowers exterior degree by one.
One has $\mu\in\mathbf F_3^{\times}$; in integer exponents we use its representative $1$ or $-1$.
The case $\mu=-1$ is impossible.
One has $\epsilon\ne0$ and $\eta/\epsilon=2$.

The $H$-Tate calculation has the following properties.*

1.

For every $\jmath\geq4$, the class $b_{\jmath}\in\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_{\mathcal A_3}^{2,4\cdot3^{\jmath+1}}
(\mathbf F_3,\mathbf F_3)$ does not survive the classical Adams spectral sequence.

On every nonzero page the class $$\label{g:Delta-unit}
 \mathcal D=\Delta b^{-6}u'^2$$ is a cycle and a unit.
Suppressing powers of $b$ and the orientation twist $u'$, the scalar and exterior-degree-three groups at $G$ have a common description $\widetilde P_n$.

At fixed $r_0,n$, the $d_5$ complex in increasing exterior degree is $$\label{g:d5-complex}
 \widetilde P_n\xrightarrow{\ r_0\operatorname{res}\ }P_n
 \xrightarrow{\ \pm(r_0+1)D\ }P_n
 \xrightarrow{\ (r_0+2)\operatorname{tr}\ }\widetilde P_n.$$
Put $$S_n=P_n/JP_{n+2},\qquad W_n=S_n\otimes\overline M.$$
After the main length-thirty-three maps, the only potential groups are those in Table 1 below, subject to the qualifications following the table.

On every residue-field entry of Table 1, including both subquotients of $\mathsf A$, a normalizing symmetry acts by $$\label{g:character-formula} d_0^{\,2m+3n+\phi},\qquad d_0^2=-1,$$ up to the same orientation-twist factor at fixed $i$, where $$\phi=0\quad\text{on scalar labels and }\mathsf x,\mathsf X, \qquad \phi=2\quad\text{on all other labels}.$$
The residue in Lemma 41 is $\rho=8$.
On page $E_R$, ordinary-to-Tate comparison is surjective in filtration $s\ge0$ and injective in filtration $s\ge R-1$, in every representation twist used here.
In [g:omega-form], one has $\omega\ne0$.
Both length-twenty-five arrows in [g:early-finite-arrows] are nonzero on every copy.
The entries $\mathsf a_0,\mathsf a_2$ and their paired $\mathsf R_0,\mathsf R_2$ are removed at length forty-nine.
All translations in $\mathcal L$ are unit cycles through page $E_{313}$.
One has $C_0=1$.

There is an element $\theta\in\pi_{322}S_{(3)}$ detected by $b_3$ in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence such that $3\theta=0$.
Let $j\geq0$ and $m=3^{j+1}$.

For a map $u:A\to B$ inducing zero in mod-three homology, the short exact sequence of Steenrod comodules $$0\longrightarrow H_*B\longrightarrow H_*C_u
   \longrightarrow \Sigma H_*A\longrightarrow0$$ is its ordinary Adams filtration-one invariant.
The reduction of the cube satisfies $$ix^3\in F^{10}\pi_{318}M.$$
The base $\mathcal B$ has cohomological dimension at most two for 3-local local coefficient systems, and $$\widetilde H^*(\mathcal B;A)=0$$ for every constant 3-local abelian group $A$.

The cone of $F:\Sigma^NM\to T$ has a nonzero operation $$\mathcal P^{81}:H^0(C_F;\mathbf F_3)\longrightarrow
 H^{N+2}(C_F;\mathbf F_3).$$

There is a unital multiplication $\mu:M\wedge M\to M$, and evaluation on the bottom cell admits a splitting $$\label{cube:end-splitting}
 \mathcal E=F(M,M)\simeq M\vee\Sigma^{-1}M.$$

Let $\widetilde E_r$ be the spectral sequence of $$\cdots\longrightarrow F_4M\longrightarrow F_3M
       \longrightarrow F_2M,$$ with absolute filtration indices retained.
There is a map $F':\Sigma^NM\to F_2T$ whose composite to $T$ has the same quotient under $\pi_T$ as $F$.
Let $I=\operatorname{fib}(S\longrightarrow\mathrm{BP})$ and $F_qZ=I^{\wedge q}\wedge Z$.
Suppose $z\in E_2^{1,108}(M)=D_{1,27}$ is a permanent cycle whose coefficient on $t_1^{27}$ is $1$.

For every parameter value $u$ one has $$K^-\subseteq\ker A(u)\subseteq K^+,
 \qquad I^-\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{im}}A(u)\subseteq I^+.$$

Let $q=b^k$ and let $t$ be a target slot.*

1.
If $\iota:B\to G_0$ sends $b$ to $bg_0$, then $$\partial^0H+H\partial^0=1-\iota\varepsilon.$$

Starting with $\partial_1=\partial^0_1$ and augmentation [alg:augmentation], the recursion $$\label{alg:deformation} \partial_sg=p- \operatorname{Ant}_{s-2}(\partial_{s-1}p;N), \qquad p=\partial^0_sg,\qquad s\geq2,$$ defines compatible finite truncations of a completed free resolution of the $\mathcal U$-module $B$.

Every actual square-zero differential satisfying the imposed Leibniz equations remains in the affine space at every refinement step.

For every actual matrix $A(u)$ in the affine family, $$K^-\subseteq\ker A(u)\subseteq K^+,
 \qquad I^-\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{im}}A(u)\subseteq I^+.$$

The recurrences and elimination instructions in this appendix give the low-cohomology ranks, the affine ranks, the sixteen enclosure rows, the sum dimensions, the two cancellation triples, the three injection tests, and the five ordinary product ranks displayed in Section 7.

outputs.exact_statement: At the prime three, $$K=K_3=\{0,2,3\}.$$ Thus the surviving classes occur in stems $10$, $106$, and $322$, and each admits an additive-order-three representative. The class $b_1$ and every $b_j$ with $j\geq4$ fail to survive.

1.  *There are homotopy equivalences of H-spaces $$\Omega S^{163}\{3\}\simeq T^{163}(3)\times\Omega T^{487}(3),
     \qquad BW_{81}\simeq\Omega T^{487}(3).$$ Consequently, $W_{81}\simeq\Omega^2T^{487}(3)$.*

2.  *For every integer $n>1$, the underlying space $\Omega S^{2n+1}\{3\}$ has a nontrivial product decomposition if and only if $n\in\{3,27,81\}$. For every other $n>1$ it is mod-three atomic, hence indecomposable. Here a product is nontrivial when both factors are noncontractible.*

3.  *For every integer $n>1$, the homotopy type $T^{2n+1}(3)$ admits a homotopy-associative H-space multiplication if and only if $n\in\{3,27,81\}$. The multiplication on $T^{163}(3)$ supplied by the displayed product is homotopy associative and homotopy commutative. For this multiplication, the third-power map on $T^{163}(3)$ is null-homotopic, as is the third-power map on the loop H-space $\Omega T^{487}(3)$.
One has $0,2\in K_3$ and $1\notin K$.

There are augmented comparisons from the ordinary Adams–Novikov spectral sequence to the mod-$3$ Adams spectral sequence and to the homotopy fixed point spectral sequences for $E^{hG}$ and $E^{hH}$. If a sphere class $\alpha$ is detected by $b_j$, then $\alpha$ has Adams–Novikov filtration exactly two. It admits a permanent representative $$x\in\mathcal N_2^{2,\,4\cdot3^{j+1}},
 \qquad \Phi(x)\in\mathbf F_3^\times b_j .$$

Let a finite group $J$ act on an even spectrum $Z$, and put $Y=Z^{hJ}$. Let $F^s=\operatorname{fib}(Y\to\mathop{\mathrm{Tot}}_{s-1}C^\bullet)$ be the decreasing tower of its group-cochain resolution. If a class in $\pi_{T-2}F^2$, with $T$ even, has nonzero symbol in $H^2(J;\pi_T Z)$, its image in $\pi_{T-2}Y$ is nonzero.

Let a finite group $J$ act on a characteristic-zero domain $A$ and semilinearly on a free rank-one module $Ae$. Suppose the kernel of $J\to\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(A)$ acts trivially on $Ae$. Then the additive trace $$\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_J:Ae\longrightarrow (Ae)^J,\qquad
 z\longmapsto\sum_{\gamma\in J}\gamma z$$ is nonzero.

Let a finite group $J$ act coherently on a spectrum $Z$. For every integer $d$, the additive trace on $\pi_d Z$ factors as $$\pi_d Z\longrightarrow \pi_d(Z^{hJ})
       \longrightarrow \pi_d Z .$$
For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, the group $\pi_{-2n}(E^{hG})$ contains an element of infinite additive order. In particular, $\pi_{-2}(E^{hG})\ne0$.
Suppose that the graded groups $\pi_*(E^{hG})$ are $972$-periodic and that $\pi_{-2}(E^{hG})$ is torsion-free. Then $b_j$ does not survive for any $j\geq4$.

Let $F^{s+1}\to F^s$, $s\geq0$, be a decreasing tower of spectra, or of genuine spectra for a finite group. If $\alpha\in\pi_VF^s$ maps to zero in $\pi_VF^0$, its layer symbol is zero by $E_{s+1}$. If that symbol is initially nonzero, its first disappearance is an incoming differential of length at most $s$.

In the cofree genuine spectra associated to $E$, the actual faithful Euler classes satisfy $$a_{\lambda|H}^{79}=0,\qquad a_\lambda^{235}=0.$$ Consequently, the $H$-Tate pages kill the unit by a differential of length at most $157$, and the $G$-Tate pages kill it by a differential of length at most $469$.

For $1\le i\le5$, the operator $D_g$ sends $P_i$ into the span of $P_0,\ldots,P_{i-1}$, with a nonzero coefficient of $P_{i-1}$. The operator $D_\sigma$ lowers the index by at least three, and its coefficient at $P_{i-3}$, for $i\ge3$, is $a^{3^{i-3}}$, where $$a\,a^{27}=-1.$$ Moreover, $D_g u/u$ has a nonzero $P_5$-term and $D_\sigma u/u$ has leading term $a^{27}P_3$. One may choose a weight-one period $u$ and linear coordinates $$y_0=[D_\sigma u/u],\qquad y_1=P_4,\qquad y_2=P_5,\qquad
 l_i=D_\sigma y_i$$ such that $$l_0=-P_0,\qquad
 \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}E_*
   =k[u^{\pm1},y_0,l_0,y_1,l_1,y_2,l_2],
 \qquad
 \sigma y_i=y_i+l_i,\quad \sigma l_i=l_i,\quad \sigma u=u.$$ The weights of $y_0,y_1,y_2$ are $0,2,8$, respectively.

There is an isomorphism of trigraded algebras $$\label{coef:first-page}
 \mathcal E_1
 =k[b^{\pm1},u^{\pm1},N_0,N_1,N_2]
       \otimes\Lambda(e,z_0,z_1,z_2).$$ Here $e,z_i$ have cohomological degree one and internal degree zero. Their cyclic cocycle values at $\sigma$ are $1,y_i$, respectively. Their $\mathfrak m$-filtrations are $0,1$, and $N_i$ has filtration three. The classes $b^{\pm1}$, $N_i$, and the class denoted $u^3$ lift to cycles of the complete coefficient complex.

After compatible nonzero scalar normalizations, the auxiliary coefficient spectral sequence has $$d_1(u)=uz_0,\qquad
 d_1(e)=ez_0,\qquad
 d_1(z_i)=z_i z_0\ (i=1,2),\qquad d_1(z_0)=0.$$ Consequently $$\label{coef:second-page}
 \mathcal E_2
 =k[b^{\pm1},u^{\pm3},N_0,N_1,N_2]
       \otimes\Lambda(eu,z_1u,z_2u,z_0).$$ Its only nonzero differential on these generators is $$d_2(z_0)=c\,bN_0,\qquad c\in k^\times.$$ There are no further differentials. In particular the leading cohomology class $eu$ is represented by an actual element $x_0\in E_{-2}$ satisfying $$x_0/u\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m},\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}_H(x_0)=0.$$ The element $x_0$ may be chosen of $T$-weight one.

Put $q_i=\mathop{\mathrm{N}}_H(x_i)$, $q=q_0$. There are norm parameters $n_1,n_2$ such that, with $K=k[[n_1,n_2]]$, $$\label{coef:h-tate-ring}
 \widehat H^*(H;E_*)=
 K[q^{\pm1},b^{\pm1}]\otimes_K\Lambda_K(V),
 \qquad |q|=(0,-6),\quad |b|=(2,0),\quad |V|=(1,4).$$ The module $V$ is free of rank three, with cyclic-cocycle basis $$a_i=x_i/q_i,\qquad 0\le i<3.$$ The group $g$ cyclically permutes this basis semilinearly over $K$. Equivalently, $q_i/q-1$, $i=1,2$, are regular parameters of $K$. For $\mathfrak n=(n_1,n_2)$, the weights on $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ are $6,-2$, and $V/\mathfrak n V$ is a single three-term Jordan block for $g$.
On every nonzero topological Tate page, $$A=qb^{-2}$$ is a permanent-cycle unit, and every element of $K$ is a cycle.

Let $B$ be an Artinian local ring with residue characteristic three, and let $F_1,F_2$ be deformations over $B$ of formal groups of finite height. A homomorphism $F_1\to F_2$ is determined by its reduction. The same assertion holds over a complete local base by passage to its Artinian quotients.

The eigenvalue condition $$\sigma x_i=\zeta x_i$$ defines a framed strict formal $\mathcal O$-module deformation space of relative height three. Its ungraded base and Lie period are $$D_0=W(k)[\zeta][[r_1,r_2]],\qquad
 r_i=x_i/x_0-1\ (i=1,2),\qquad w=x_0.$$ The full ungraded $H$-fixed base is equivalently $$\label{coef:nonreduced-fixed}
 W(k)[[s,r_1,r_2]]/(s^2+3s+3),\qquad 1+s=\sigma x_0/x_0.$$ In particular its characteristic-three fibre retains the relation $s^2=0$.*

*Set $\bar D=D_0/(\pi)$. There is a $\mathcal C$-invariant Hasse section $h_1$ in the line $w^{-2}$, given by the first strict coefficient of $\sigma$. On its zero divisor there is a $\mathcal C$-invariant Hasse section $h$ in $w^{-8}$, given by the second strict coefficient. The ring $$D'=\bar D/(h_1)$$ is a formal disc with parameter $hw^8$; here ideals generated by line sections are read after a period trivialization.*

*Evaluation in cyclic cohomology and reduction modulo $\pi$ identify $$K\cong\bar D^{\,3},\qquad q\longmapsto w^3.$$ The evaluated $V$ is the $\bar D^3$-span of $1,x_1/x_0,x_2/x_0$ in the line $w^{-2}$. There is a $\mathcal C$-fixed primitive element $\theta\in V$, the restriction of the class of $t_1$, which evaluates to $h_1$ up to a nonzero scalar.*


*One may choose a $T$-basis $v,\theta,y$ of $V$ with weights $-2,0,6$, with $v=x_0/q$. Modulo $\mathfrak n$, $$\label{coef:jordan}
 g\theta=\theta,\qquad
 gy=y+c_1\theta,\qquad
 gv=v+c_2y+c_3\theta,\qquad c_1c_2\ne0.$$ Using evaluation to identify cube sections with their unique preimages, put $$J=h_1^3\in Kq^{-2},\qquad F=q^2J,\qquad
 S_0=K/(F)\cong(D')^3,\qquad
 W=(V/K\theta)\otimes_K S_0.$$ Then $F$ is a regular parameter of $K$, and there is an injective $\mathcal C$-equivariant evaluation $$W\longrightarrow w^{-2}\quad\text{over }D'.$$ After trivializing the line, the evaluations of $v,y$ have orders zero and one, respectively.

Every open subgroup of $\mathcal C$ has infinite image on $D'$. Its invariant Laurent functions are constants. These assertions remain valid after a finite extension of the residue field, with the group acting trivially on the extended constants.

A nonzero invariant meromorphic section of $w^i$ is a constant multiple of $h^d$, where $8d=-i$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$. If it is integral, then $d\ge0$. There is no nonzero invariant meromorphic section of $w^i\chi$ for any nontrivial constant sign character $\chi:\mathcal C\to\{\pm1\}$.

After a finite extension of constants there is an equivariant isomorphism $$\label{coef:determinant-formula}
 \det(D'\otimes_{S_0}W)\cong w^{-9}\chi,$$ where $\chi:\mathcal C\to\{\pm1\}$ is a sign character whose restriction to $T$ has weight $13$, and is therefore nontrivial.

For every integer $n$, including after meromorphic localization, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal C,S_0}(W,P_n)=0.$$ Every nonzero invariant integral vector in $WP_n$ evaluates as a constant multiple of $h^d$, where $$8d=2-3n,\qquad d\ge0.$$ If $h$ occurs in $WP_{-2}$, the corresponding line $$\ell=hP_2\subset W$$ is primitive and stable. After extension to $D'$, its quotient has character $w^{-15}\chi$. More generally, if $h^{1+3k}$ occurs in $WP_{-2-8k}$, $k\ge0$, then $h$ already occurs in $WP_{-2}$.

With compatible nonzero scalar normalizations, the images of the indicated Greek-letter classes are $$\alpha_1=\theta,\qquad
  \beta_1=bJ,\qquad
  \beta_{3/3}=bJ^3,\qquad
  \beta_4=\pm bJ^5.$$ In particular, $$\label{h:d5-b}
  d_5(b)=\theta b^3,\qquad d_5(\theta)=0.$$

On the cohomology of [h:sector-complex], the operation $\kappa=A^2d_9$ preserves both the $A$- and $b$-exponents and lowers exterior degree by one. It is a derivation and satisfies $$\label{h:kappa-theta} \kappa(\Theta)=cF,\qquad c\in k^{\times}.$$
The case $\mu=-1$ is impossible.

The $H$-Tate calculation has the following properties.* 1. *The first differential is $$d_5(b^m q^n\xi) =(m+2n+2j)b^{m+2}q^n\theta\wedge\xi, \qquad \xi\in\Lambda^jV,$$ up to a single nonzero scalar normalization. Its cohomology has generators $A,B=b^3,\Theta=b^{-1}\theta$ and $b^{-2}(V/K\theta)$ as in [h:e6], with $\mu=1$. For a fixed $c\in k^{\times}$, the next differential is $$d_9(\Theta)=cA^{-2}F=cb^4J.$$ Equivalently, on surviving $\Theta$-containing representatives, $$d_9\bigl([b^m q^n\theta\wedge\xi]\bigr) =c[b^{m+5}q^nJ\xi],$$ where $\xi$ is a complementary exterior monomial. These raw products are interpreted in the $A,B$ normal form: $A^{-2}$ is a surviving unit, while $b^4$ and $J$ need not survive separately. Its cohomology is [h:e10].* 2. *The $d_{17}$ is wedge multiplication by the invariant Hasse vector $h$, with common unit shifts and coefficients $p$ on exterior degree zero and $p-1$ on exterior degree one. Its survivors have supports $$\begin{array}{c|c} \text{component}&p\pmod3\\\hline \text{scalars}&0\\ \ell&2\\ W/\ell&1\\ \det W&0. \end{array}$$* 3. *The nonzero $d_{33}$ contracts $\ell$ to scalars and $\det W$ to $W/\ell$. Under the identifications by $h$ and $h\wedge(-)$, respectively, these maps are multiplication by $h^3$, up to nonzero scalar units and the prescribed degree shifts. Only scalars at $p\equiv0$ and quotient classes at $p\equiv1$ remain, now over $S_0/(Z)=k$.* 4. *The remaining algebra and differentials are [h:e34], [h:d53], and [h:d105]. The coefficient $e_{53}$ has not been asserted nonzero in this subgroup calculation.

For every $\jmath\geq4$, the class $b_{\jmath}\in\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}_{\mathcal A_3}^{2,4\cdot3^{\jmath+1}}
(\mathbf F_3,\mathbf F_3)$ does not survive the classical Adams spectral sequence.

On every nonzero page the class $$\label{g:Delta-unit}
 \mathcal D=\Delta b^{-6}u'^2$$ is a cycle and a unit. Constants from $W(k)$ act by cycles. There is also a semilinear symmetry commuting with $G$, inducing Witt Frobenius on $k$ and fixing $b$ and $u'$.

Suppressing powers of $b$ and the orientation twist $u'$, the scalar and exterior-degree-three groups at $G$ have a common description $\widetilde P_n$. Restriction fits into $$0\longrightarrow \overline k_n\longrightarrow
 \widetilde P_n\xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}}P_n^Q
 \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \overline k_n=
 \begin{cases}k,&3\mid n,\\0,&3\nmid n.
 \end{cases}$$ Transfer embeds $(P_n)_Q$ in $\widetilde P_n$, with cokernel $\overline k_n$. Moreover $$\label{g:P-tate}
 \widehat H^d(Q;P_n)=\overline k_n
 \qquad(d\in\mathbf Z).$$ For $3\mid n$, the exceptional class is represented by $\Delta^{n/3}$; its transfer is the nonzero three-multiple in the restriction kernel. There is a class $c_G$ restricting to $a_0a_1a_2$, and multiplication by $c_G$ identifies the scalar and volume descriptions, including their exceptional kernels.*

*In exterior degrees one and two, restriction is injective onto all invariants. These groups are parametrized by transfer of $P_na_0$ and $P_na_0a_1$, respectively.

Put $$S_n=P_n/JP_{n+2},\qquad W_n=S_n\otimes\overline M.$$ The main $H$ groups on $E_{10}$ are $S_n,W_n,S_n$ in exterior degrees $0,1,2$, respectively, at $w_0\equiv0\pmod3$. Define transfer modules $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_n&=
 \begin{cases}(S_n)_Q,&n\equiv0,2\pmod3,\\
 NS_n,&n\equiv1\pmod3,
 \end{cases}\label{g:Tn}\\
 \mathcal W_n&=
 \begin{cases}(W_n)_Q,&n\equiv1,2\pmod3,\\
 NW_n,&n\equiv0\pmod3.
 \end{cases}\label{g:Wn}
\end{aligned}$$ At $G$ the main groups are:*

1.  *in degree zero, a scalar group $\mathcal S_n$ with transfer part $\mathcal T_n$ and one additional restriction generator when $3\mid n$;*

2.  *in degree one, the transfer group $\mathcal W_n$;*

3.  *in degree two, the transfer group $\mathcal T_n$.*

*On these transfer groups restriction is norm and transfer is the displayed projection. The additional groups are one $k$ each, only when $3\mid n$: scalar restriction kernels at $w_0\equiv1,2\pmod3$, and volume groups at every $w_0$. The volume is of $3c_G$ kernel type when $w_0\equiv1$, and of reduced $c_G$ type when $w_0\equiv0,2$.

Put $T_0=b^5c_G$ on $E_{13}$. After a nonzero normalization, $$d_{13}B/B=\varepsilon T_0,\qquad
 d_{13}u'/u'=0,\qquad \varepsilon\ne0.$$ There is a residue $\rho\in\{2,5,8\}\pmod9$ such that the extra scalar families surviving $d_{13}$ occur in the two families $w_0\equiv1\pmod3$ or $w_0\equiv\rho\pmod9$. The extra volume families occur in the three residue families $$w_0\equiv0\pmod3,\qquad 2\pmod9,
 \qquad \rho+2\pmod9.$$ Scalar generators outside the transfer part survive precisely at $w_0=9t$ and $3\mid n$.
After the main length-thirty-three maps, the only potential groups are those in Table 1 below, subject to the qualifications following the table.
The residue in Lemma 41 is $ ho=8$. The coefficient $e_{53}$ of the $H$ length-fifty-three differential is nonzero. Moreover, in [g:V-form] one has $ u e0$ and $ u'=0$.

On page $E_R$, ordinary-to-Tate comparison is surjective in filtration $s\ge0$ and injective in filtration $s\ge R-1$, in every representation twist used here. If a specified ordinary filtration-zero symbol is a Tate cycle through length $R-1$, then it extends as an ordinary class over the $(R-1)$-skeleton.
In [g:omega-form], one has $\omega\ne0$.
Both length-twenty-five arrows in [g:early-finite-arrows] are nonzero on every copy. Thus $\mathsf b,\mathsf v,\mathsf d,\mathsf r$ are all removed at that length.

All translations in $\mathcal L$ are unit cycles through page $E_{313}$. The unit is hit at length $313$ from the $\mathsf f$ translate $$\label{g:last-f}
 (-5,-36)+\mathcal L.$$ There are no other arrows on the remaining labels at that length, and the next page is zero.

For a map $u:A\to B$ inducing zero in mod-three homology, the short exact sequence of Steenrod comodules $$0\longrightarrow H_*B\longrightarrow H_*C_u
   \longrightarrow \Sigma H_*A\longrightarrow0$$ is its ordinary Adams filtration-one invariant. This invariant is natural and additive in $u$. It vanishes for a composite of two maps that induce zero in mod-three homology, and hence for a map of Adams–Novikov filtration at least two.

 \qquad I^-\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{im}}A(u)\subseteq I^+.$$

Let $q=b^k$ and let $t$ be a target slot.*

1.  *If multiplication by $q$ is surjective into $D_t$ and injective into $D_{t+J}$, it is surjective into $H_t$.*

2.  *If it is injective into $D_t$ and surjective into $D_{t-J}$, it is injective into $H_t$.
If $\iota:B\to G_0$ sends $b$ to $bg_0$, then $$\partial^0H+H\partial^0=1-\iota\varepsilon.$$ The map $H$ preserves the coefficient $v^Q$, the number $|T|+w(g)$, and the tuple $T+C(g)$.

Starting with $\partial_1=\partial^0_1$ and augmentation [alg:augmentation], the recursion $$\label{alg:deformation} \partial_sg=p- \operatorname{Ant}_{s-2}(\partial_{s-1}p;N), \qquad p=\partial^0_sg,\qquad s\geq2,$$ defines compatible finite truncations of a completed free resolution of the $\mathcal U$-module $B$. Every call to [alg:antidifferential] terminates. Cochains of internal weight $d\leq N$ in this resolution calculate the ordinary normalized-cobar cohomology $D_{s,d}$.

The rule [alg:product] calculates signed Yoneda products, with the first factor lifted first. It is independent on cohomology of all choices of lifts and representatives. It agrees with the ordinary Ext product with the corresponding ordering convention. If the cobar comparison instead uses the ordinary opposite ordering of the two factors, graded commutativity changes the product formula by $(-1)^{jf}$ for factors of filtrations $j$ and $f$. For every actual matrix $A(u)$ in the affine family, $$K^-\subseteq\ker A(u)\subseteq K^+,
 \qquad I^-\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{im}}A(u)\subseteq I^+.$$ These inclusions remain valid when parameters shared with other matrices are correlated or satisfy further equations.
